Then the 9 getsockopt assertions: (1) fd 400/SOL_SOCKET/SO_OOBINLINE -> EBADF(9); (2) /dev/null fd -> ENOTSOCK(88); (3) optval=NULL -> EFAULT(14); (4) optlen=NULL -> EFAULT(14); (5) level=500 -> EOPNOTSUPP(95); (6) level=IPPROTO_UDP -> EOPNOTSUPP(95); (7) IPPROTO_IP/optname=-1 -> ENOPROTOOPT(92); (8) IPPROTO_TCP/optname=-1 -> ENOPROTOOPT(92); (9) optlen=(socklen_t)-1 -> EINVAL(22).
failing_assertion: Not a getsockopt assertion at all -- the test aborts in setup() before any of the 9 cases execute. With KIRK_VERBOSE=1 the guest reports: 'getsockopt01.c:82: TBROK: bind(4, 0.0.0.0, 16) failed: EADDRNOTAVAIL (99)'. That is getsockopt01.c:82, the SAFE_BIND(sock_bind, &sin0, sizeof(sin0)) with sin0.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY. Asterinas returns -1/EADDRNOTAVAIL(99) where the correct kernel returns 0. kirk therefore scores the test 'broken (0.012s)' with passed 0 / failed 0 / broken 1, and run_ltp_test.sh:36-39 treats broken != 0 as failure. Zero of the 9 getsockopt assertions were ever reached, so nothing is currently known about their correctness on Asterinas.
root_cause: bind(2) on an INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0) IPv4 address is not implemented. The path is sys_bind -> StreamSocket::bind (kernel/src/net/socket/ip/stream/mod.rs:470-479) -> InitStream::bind (kernel/src/net/socket/ip/stream/init.rs:88-105) -> bind_port (init.rs:276-279) -> resolve_bind_iface_and_config (kernel/src/net/socket/ip/common.rs:80-99). At common.rs:86 that function calls get_iface_to_bind (common.rs:17-34), which resolves an interface by requiring an *exact equality* match between the requested address and an interface's configured CIDR address: `iface.ipv4_cidr().is_some_and(|cidr| cidr.address() == ipv4_addr)`. The only two interfaces are created in kernel/src/net/iface/init.rs:35-48 -- loopback with 127.0.0.1/8 (init.rs:68-69) and the virtio iface with the DHCP/static address. Neither has address 0.0.0.0, so the wildcard matches no interface, get_iface_to_bind returns None, and common.rs:88-93 takes the `None =>` arm returning EADDRNOTAVAIL with message 'the address is not available from the local machine'. This is not an oversight in that function but the documented consequence of a deeper design limitation: the socket table is per-interface rather than per-netns, and a wildcard bind has no single interface to belong to. kernel/libs/aster-bigtcp/src/socket_table.rs:44-48 states 'this table is currently limited to a single interface. TODO: Modify the table to be shared across a single network namespace to support INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0)', and socket_table.rs:50-54 states 'Linux has two hashtables for listeners... The second table is the only place where sockets listening on INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0) can exist. Since we do not yet support INADDR_ANY, we only have the first table here.' ListenerKey::new (socket_table.rs:34-38) carries the matching 'FIXME: If the socket is listening on an unspecified address (0.0.0.0), Linux will get the hash value by port only.' kernel/src/net/socket/ip/stream/init.rs:205-206 independently confirms the gap: 'FIXME: The socket should be bound to INADDR_ANY (i.e., 0.0.0.0) with an ephemeral port. However, INADDR_ANY is not yet supported, so we need to return an error first.' Supporting the wildcard therefore requires a netns-scoped socket table plus a second port-keyed listener hashtable and wildcard-aware packet demultiplexing -- a networking-subsystem change, not a localized defect. Note this also invalidates the select phase's premise: select predicted a validation-order defect inside the 47-line kernel/src/syscall/getsockopt.rs, but that file is never reached by this test. Its analysis of getsockopt.rs is untested here and the one genuinely additive item it identified (no optlen upper-bound check exists in getsockopt.rs, so tcase 9's EINVAL is likely still absent) remains unverified because setup aborts first.
invariant: bind(2) with the IPv4 wildcard address INADDR_ANY (0.0.0.0) succeeds on any host that has at least one usable interface, and binds the socket to the given port on all local addresses rather than to one interface's address. The wildcard is not an interface address and must never be resolved by matching it against configured interface addresses.
owning_layer: The IP socket layer's bind address resolution, kernel/src/net/socket/ip/common.rs (resolve_bind_iface_and_config / get_iface_to_bind), backed by the port/socket bookkeeping in kernel/libs/aster-bigtcp/src/socket_table.rs. Asterinas's abstractions do not line up with Linux's here: Linux keeps one inet hashtable per network namespace, so a wildcard listener is naturally namespace-scoped and interface-independent, whereas Asterinas keys its SocketTable and PortTable per Iface (socket_table.rs:44-48), which structurally forces every bind to name exactly one interface. The closest equivalent layer is therefore the ip socket module's bind resolution, but a correct fix cannot live there alone -- common.rs cannot honestly answer 'which iface' for 0.0.0.0, so the table must first become namespace-scoped (or a wildcard/all-ifaces binding must become representable) before common.rs can stop rejecting the wildcard. Patching only common.rs, e.g. by silently redirecting 0.0.0.0 to the loopback or virtio iface, would make this test's setup pass while leaving the socket reachable on just one interface -- the exact wrong-layer failure this field exists to prevent, since a wildcard listener that misses packets on the other interface is a silently wrong bind rather than an honest error.
linux_reference: net/ipv4/af_inet.c __inet_bind (v6.12, lines 473-507, read from raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12): it computes chk_addr_ret = inet_addr_type_table(...) and then rejects with -EADDRNOTAVAIL only if !inet_addr_valid_or_nonlocal(net, inet, addr->sin_addr.s_addr, chk_addr_ret). That helper, in include/net/inet_sock.h lines 430-440, is `return inet_can_nonlocal_bind(net, inet) || addr == htonl(INADDR_ANY) || addr_type == RTN_LOCAL || addr_type == RTN_MULTICAST || addr_type == RTN_BROADCAST;`. So Linux special-cases the wildcard *explicitly and unconditionally*, in the AF_INET socket layer, before and independently of any per-interface address lookup -- INADDR_ANY short-circuits the local-address check rather than being resolved to an interface. Placement matters: this is enforced in the protocol/socket layer (af_inet), above any device, which is why the rule belongs in Asterinas's ip socket bind path rather than inside per-iface matching. Linux then stores the wildcard in inet->inet_rcv_saddr and hashes such listeners by port only in the second listener hashtable, which is precisely the structure socket_table.rs:50-54 records as absent.
other_callers: Widely reached, which is what makes this a subsystem gap rather than a one-test curiosity. The same resolve_bind_iface_and_config is the single bind-address resolver for both TCP and UDP: kernel/src/net/socket/ip/stream/init.rs:277 (bind_port for stream sockets) and kernel/src/net/socket/ip/datagram/unbound.rs:78 (bind_port for datagram sockets), so every AF_INET bind of either protocol hits the identical wildcard rejection. Consequently any server that binds 0.0.0.0 -- the overwhelmingly common idiom -- cannot start on Asterinas. The related listen()-without-bind() path is already broken for the same reason and returns EINVAL with warn!("listen() without bind() is not implemented") at init.rs:205-211. Within the LTP pool alone, 23 currently-commented-out tests in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt reference INADDR_ANY and would hit this same defect: accept01, accept02, accept03, accept4_01, bind01, bind02, bind05, connect01, connect02, epoll_wait05, getpeername01, getsockname01, getsockopt01, recv01, recvfrom01, recvmsg01, send01, sendmsg01, sendto01, setsockopt01, shutdown02, socketcall03, sockioctl01. That clustering is the strongest argument for fixing this at the socket/table layer: one correct wildcard implementation would unblock the whole group, whereas a per-test workaround unblocks none of the others. Notably the in-tree regression test test/initramfs/src/regression/network/tcp_server.c does *not* exercise the gap -- it sets INADDR_ANY at line 34 but then overwrites the address with inet_pton(AF_INET, "127.0.0.1", ...) at line 38, binding a concrete address, which is why the missing wildcard support has gone unnoticed by the regression suite.
suggested_direction: Do not attempt to fix this within this run's scope as a getsockopt change; getsockopt.rs is not on the failing path. The correct fix is to implement IPv4 wildcard bind in the IP socket layer: (1) make the socket/port tables namespace-scoped rather than per-iface, or introduce an explicit 'bound to all interfaces' binding that the per-iface tables can represent, per the TODO at kernel/libs/aster-bigtcp/src/socket_table.rs:44-48; (2) add the second port-keyed listener hashtable so wildcard listeners can be hashed by port only, per socket_table.rs:50-54 and the ListenerKey FIXME at socket_table.rs:34-38; (3) in resolve_bind_iface_and_config (kernel/src/net/socket/ip/common.rs:80-99), special-case the unspecified address before calling get_iface_to_bind, mirroring inet_addr_valid_or_nonlocal, so 0.0.0.0 is accepted without an interface lookup instead of falling into the None arm; (4) make packet demultiplexing consult wildcard listeners on every interface. Because that is a multi-part networking-subsystem change touching aster-bigtcp's table design, it exceeds the localized-defect scope this run was selected for and the run should be retired as missing-feature rather than fixed. A future run that lands wildcard bind should re-run getsockopt01 and then separately evaluate the 9 getsockopt assertions, since tcase 9 (optlen=(socklen_t)-1 -> EINVAL) has no bound check anywhere in kernel/src/syscall/getsockopt.rs and may well still fail once setup() succeeds. Also note for whoever does this: KIRK_VERBOSE is read by test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/run_ltp_test.sh:23 but is not plumbed through the root Makefile to the guest, so the default run reports only 'broken (0.012s)' and hides the TBROK reason; I temporarily defaulted it to 1 to read the failure and have reverted that edit (worktree is clean).
